text: A topological space is called ___ (the T₂ separation axiom) if any two distinct points possess disjoint open neighbourhoods; the book imposes this on smooth manifolds so that distinct spacetime events are topologically distinguishable.
explanation: The Hausdorff (T₂) condition separates distinct points by disjoint open sets; in such spaces limits of sequences are unique and compact subsets are closed. The 'line with two origins' is the standard non-Hausdorff counterexample the book excludes from being a manifold.
